name: Suehirocho
tagline: Tokyo in 10 minutes and Otemachi in 12 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 12 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 27 minutes to Shibuya and 24 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 3.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 7.7 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.6 m to 10.3 m, a difference of 7.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 6 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 5 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 72 clinics and 58 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 萩原医院, about 4 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東都文京病院, about 7 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000 and 2LDK ¥280,000 to ¥290,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Akihabara is ahead on the number of lines, but Suehirocho is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Suehirocho. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Suehirocho.

noiseSources: The 首都高速1号上野線 viaduct runs a short walk from the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
中央通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 27 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
